page_title: Yalqen — Open-source Chromium browser for Mac developers

sources.entry: Yalqen - Open-source Chromium browser for developers with vertical tabs, a keyboard-first command bar, built-in developer tools, and ad and tracker blocking. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/YSamed/yalqen) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: Yalqen
summary.one_liner: Yalqen is a free, open-source Chromium browser for Mac developers, featuring vertical tabs, a keyboard command bar, built-in developer tools and ad blocking.
use_cases: Testing web pages at phone sizes and in dark mode
Inspecting and debugging network requests with DevTools
Mocking or redirecting requests during web development
Working on web projects with an AI assistant beside the page
Browsing with vertical tabs and keyboard shortcuts
Blocking ads and trackers without installing an extension
summary.what_it_does: Yalqen is a Chromium-based browser for macOS aimed at web developers. Tabs sit in a foldable side panel that can be shown, hidden or resized, and a command bar on ⌘L searches tabs, history and commands. It includes Chromium DevTools plus built-in tools such as request rules to block, mock, redirect or rewrite headers, per-tab network throttling and full-page screenshots. A phone view mode provides device presets and can emulate dark mode and reduced motion. It runs Chrome Web Store extensions and offers an AI panel that works with Claude, Codex or Gemini alongside the page.
notable: Vertical tabs with a command bar on ⌘L and keyboard-driven layout controls
Built-in developer tools: request rules, network throttling, phone view emulation
Runs on Chromium and supports Chrome Web Store extensions
Open source under the MIT license with a built-in AI panel for Claude, Codex or Gemini
caveats: Mac only; the page lists macOS 13+ and Apple silicon, and asks about Intel Mac support in its FAQ without stating the answer on the page
